import pandas as pd

# File paths for the source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_69/test_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_69/test_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_69/test_2.csv"

# Load source tables
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path)  # Columns: ['user_id', 'year_school', 'floor']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path)  # Columns: ['user_id', 'party', 'libcon']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path)  # Columns: ['user_id', 'fav_music']

# Step 1: Merge df0 and df1 on 'user_id' using inner join to keep only users present in both
df_01 = pd.merge(df0, df1, on='user_id', how='inner')

# Step 2: Merge the result with df2 on 'user_id' using inner join to keep only users present in all three
df_final = pd.merge(df_01, df2, on='user_id', how='inner')

# Step 3: Ensure the columns are in the target schema order and types
# Target schema: ['user_id': int, 'year_school': str, 'floor': str, 'party': str, 'libcon': str, 'fav_music': str]

# Convert user_id to integer explicitly (in case of float due to CSV reading)
df_final['user_id'] = df_final['user_id'].astype(int)

# Convert all other columns to string type
for col in ['year_school', 'floor', 'party', 'libcon', 'fav_music']:
    df_final[col] = df_final[col].astype(str)

# Reorder columns to match target schema
df_final = df_final[['user_id', 'year_school', 'floor', 'party', 'libcon', 'fav_music']]

# Step 4: Write the final dataframe to the target CSV file
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_69/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_final.to_csv(target_path, index=False)
